Canada has made its Rural Community Immigration Pilot a permanent programme, creating a continuing pathway to attract and retain skilled foreign workers in smaller communities facing persistent labour shortages. The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Lena Metlege Diab, announced the decision on Monday, November 9, 2026, in Pictou County, Nova Scotia. According to a release on Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) website, the programme will initially continue with the 14 communities currently participating in the pilot, with plans to expand to additional communities in the future. The employer- and community-led initiative is designed to address the distinct workforce needs of rural Canada by connecting newcomers and their families with local employers and community support systems to encourage long-term settlement. Announcing the decision, Diab said the government recognised the importance of rural communities to the country’s economy and the challenges they face in finding workers. “Our government understands that rural communities play a critical role in powering Canada’s economy. At the same time, many face real challenges finding the workers they need. “That’s why we’re transitioning our successful rural immigration pilot into a permanent program—helping smaller communities attract and retain essential workers who deliver services and drive economic growth. “We appreciate that a one-size-fits-all approach to immigration doesn’t work for rural Canada, and this permanent pathway is one part of our work to ensure that communities of all sizes can share in the benefits of responsible, sustainable immigration,” she said. The government said the programme would complement its efforts to stabilise immigration admissions, reduce the temporary resident population and retain skilled workers already living and contributing to communities across the country. What the programme has achieved IRCC said the permanent programme builds on the Rural and Northern Immigration Pilot, which ran from 2019 to 2024, and the Rural Community Immigration Pilot, introduced in 2025. More than 2,800 employers participated in the earlier Rural and Northern Immigration Pilot, resulting in over 12,500 candidates and their family members being admitted to smaller and rural communities across Canada. Between January 2025 and August 2026, participating communities vetted and designated more than 1,950 trusted employers facing persistent labour shortages that could not be filled locally. The employers subsequently issued more than 4,700 job offers and community recommendations. The Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada, Sean Fraser, said the programme had helped businesses in Pictou County retain workers and encouraged newcomers to establish permanent roots in the community. “We’ve seen the difference this program makes here in Pictou County. It’s helping local businesses keep workers they need, people who’ve become our neighbours and friends, and want to build their lives here. “We’re one of 14 communities that have helped make this pilot work. “Now we’re making it permanent, so businesses can count on it when they can’t fill jobs locally, and these families can keep calling our community home,” Fraser said. Similarly, the Secretary of State for Rural Development, Buckley Belanger, said the programme recognised the different labour needs of rural, northern and remote communities. He said strategic immigration pathways could help address workforce shortages where locally available Canadian workers could not fill vacancies. The Chief Executive Officer of Pictou County Partnership, Jason Guidry, also said the programme had strengthened the local workforce, supported business growth and helped welcome new residents. Meanwhile, IRCC said eligibility criteria for additional communities that may join the programme in future would be communicated through a separate announcement. The department also identified the Provincial Nominee Program and federal economic immigration programmes managed through Express Entry as other pathways available to skilled workers seeking permanent residence in Canada.
